area: App shell, navigation, login, settings, theming

screens.name: App shell (header, sidebar navigation, page frame, footer)
screens.route: Wrapper rendered by every authenticated page via <AppShell title> (17 call sites: /my-work, /incidents, /event-groups, /event-groups/:id, /assessments, /mission-center, /gis/terrain-cross-sections, /submissions, /submissions/:id, /submissions/:id/photo-evidence, /admin/users, /admin/road-inventory, /settings). Not a layout route: each page mounts its own AppShell (web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:131).
screens.purpose: Frame every authenticated page with the ERIS brand header, a role-filtered section navigation, signed-in identity + Sign out, a quick theme switch, and a titled content card.
roles: All authenticated roles see the shell; nav sections vary by role (AppShell.tsx:72-104)
Workspace › My Work: operational roles only (hasWorkQueue = isOperationalUser; roleModel.ts:71-73)

Operations › Mission Center / Event Groups / Assessments: OPERATIONAL_ROLE_NAMES (MAINTENANCE_COORDINATOR, GEOTECH_OFFICE_CHIEF, GEOTECH_BRANCH_CHIEF, GEOTECH_ENGINEER + legacy aliases, REVIEWER, ADMIN)
Operations › Incidents: every role incl. MAINTENANCE_FIELD_WORKER/MAINTENANCE (AppShell.tsx:86)
GIS Tools › Terrain Cross Sections: operational roles (AppShell.tsx:90-92)
Administration › Users / Road Inventory: ADMIN only (AppShell.tsx:93-101)
primaryTasks: Move between ERIS areas (My Work, Operations records, GIS tools, Admin, Settings)
Confirm who is signed in and with which roles, then sign out
Switch the colour theme without leaving the current page

entryPoints: Any authenticated route renders AppShell (17 <AppShell title=...> call sites)
Deep links to any route survive ProtectedRoute after AuthGateLoading

No breadcrumbs, no home link on logo, no 'back' affordance in the shell; detail pages must supply their own

responsive.layout: Sticky header (z-20, backdrop-blur) + max-w-[1900px] container. Below lg: flex-col with a full-width 'Navigation' card stacked above <main>. lg+: flex-row with a sticky (top-[82px]) sidebar fixed at w-64 (256px) or w-16 (64px) when collapsed, then <main min-w-0 flex-1>. Content is wrapped in .product-card overflow-hidden. workspace=true (TerrainCrossSectionsPage only) switches to lg:h-screen lg:overflow-hidden, tighter gaps and no footer (AppShell.tsx:138,163-189).
breakpointsUsed: md:block / md:px-6 — identity block shown and wider gutters at ≥768px (AppShell.tsx:140,157,163,189)
lg:hidden / lg:block / lg:flex-row / lg:h-screen / lg:overflow-hidden / lg:min-h-0 / lg:gap-4|6 — sidebar vs stacked nav flips at ≥1024px (AppShell.tsx:138,163-165,183-185)
Fixed widths: w-64, w-16, h-9 w-9 logo, h-8 w-8 toggle, h-10 w-10 collapsed items, max-w-64 name, max-w-[1900px], sticky top-[82px]
Overflow handling: min-w-0 + truncate on title/subtitle/name/nav labels; product-card overflow-hidden on content
No xl/2xl usage; Tailwind v4 default breakpoints (no @theme override found in web/)
phoneRisks: 375px: the entire navigation renders as a card ABOVE the page content on every page (AppShell.tsx:164). An admin sees 5 section headings + 9 links (~430px) before the page title — the primary content starts below the fold and there is no hamburger/drawer/collapse on <lg.

Identity block (name + roles) hidden below md (AppShell.tsx:157) and theme select hidden below sm (AppShell.tsx:146): on a phone there is no indication who is signed in, and theme can only be changed from Settings.
Header title 'Emergency Response Information System' (text-sm) truncates to roughly 'Emergency Response Inf…' next to the 36px logo and Sign out button (AppShell.tsx:143).
Touch targets: nav items are px-3 py-2 text-sm (≈36px tall), Sign out ≈38px, both under the 44px guideline (AppShell.tsx:39,158).
tabletRisks: 768–1023px (iPad portrait, most Android tablets): still the stacked-nav phone layout because the sidebar only appears at lg (1024px) (AppShell.tsx:164-165) — a large nav card wastes the top of every page.

At exactly 1024px (iPad landscape): sidebar appears; main content width ≈ 1024 − 48 (px-6) − 256 − 24 (gap) ≈ 696px, which is tight for pages that lay out lg:grid-cols-5 summary cards or wide tables. Collapsing to w-16 helps but the collapsed state is lost on every navigation (AppShell.tsx:134).
sticky top-[82px] is a magic number tied to the current header height; if the header wraps or the brand text changes height the sidebar overlaps or gaps (AppShell.tsx:166).
desktopNotes: Sidebar 256px expanded / 64px collapsed with 200ms width transition; collapsed items are 40x40 icon buttons with title + aria-label (AppShell.tsx:39,45-46,165).

Because every page mounts its own <AppShell>, header and sidebar re-render on each route change: collapse state resets to expanded, no persisted preference, and no shared layout state (AppShell.tsx:131-134; all 17 call sites).
Container caps at 1900px so ultra-wide monitors get centered content with side margins.

painPoints.issue: No responsive navigation pattern below lg: the full nav list is stacked above content on phone and tablet, pushing the page title and content below the fold on every page.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:164 (aside lg:hidden renders <SidebarNavigation /> as a card) and :165 (sidebar only at lg:block)

painPoints.issue: Sidebar collapse state is not persisted; it resets to expanded on every navigation because each page mounts its own AppShell with local useState.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:134 (useState(true)); 17 per-page <AppShell> call sites (e.g. SettingsPage.tsx:26, MyWorkPage.tsx:120)

painPoints.issue: Raw role enum codes are shown to the user in the header ('GEOTECH_OFFICE_CHIEF · ADMIN'); there is no shared human-readable role label.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:157; only local helper is AdminUsersOperationsPage.tsx:8-10; roleModel.ts has assessmentStateLabel (81-93) but no role label map

painPoints.issue: On phones the shell shows no signed-in identity at all (name and roles are md:block) and no theme control (sm:flex).
Logo and product name are not a link; there is no 'home' affordance in the shell and no breadcrumbs, so users rely on the nav list alone.
Header theme select labels (Light/Dark/Coastal) differ from Settings labels (Caltrans Light/Dark/Coastal Teal); the option list is duplicated in two files.
Nav item highlighted through alsoActive (Assessments while on /submissions/*) gets the active style but not aria-current='page', so screen-reader users and visual users disagree on location.
Nav links, Sign out and the theme select rely on browser-default focus outlines while form inputs elsewhere use a custom brand ring; nav/sign-out touch targets are below 44px.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:38-43,152,158 (no focus-visible classes; py-2 / py-1.5 sizes)

painPoints.issue: No skip-to-content link; on phone a keyboard/switch user must tab through every nav item before reaching content.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:137-190 (no skip link; grep for 'Skip to' found nothing)

painPoints.issue: Footer copyright repeats boilerplate on every page and disappears in workspace mode, making the footer presence inconsistent.

strengths: Role-filtered information architecture is documented inline and implemented in one hook (AppShell.tsx:63-104), so users never see areas they cannot use.
Collapsed sidebar keeps accessibility: sr-only section labels, per-link title + aria-label, aria-expanded on the toggle (AppShell.tsx:45-46,57,171-173).
Header is sticky with translucent backdrop-blur and z-20, keeping Sign out and theme reachable while scrolling (AppShell.tsx:139).
Overflow discipline: min-w-0 + truncate on every text block prevents header blow-out (AppShell.tsx:141-143,157).
workspace mode gives map-heavy pages a viewport-locked frame without a footer (AppShell.tsx:138,163,185,189).
All colours come from CSS custom properties, so the shell re-themes instantly across light/dark/coastal (index.css:9-58).

responsive.layout: Full-viewport <main> with a centred max-w-6xl card. Card is a CSS grid: single column below lg; lg:grid-cols-[1.15fr_0.85fr] with a hidden-until-lg brand/marketing panel on the left and the form (max-w-md, centred) on the right. Both sections have min-h-[620px] (LoginPage.tsx:51-53,54,77).
breakpointsUsed: sm:px-6 / sm:p-10 — gutters and form padding (LoginPage.tsx:51,77)
lg:px-8, lg:grid-cols-[1.15fr_0.85fr], lg:flex (brand panel), lg:hidden (mobile brand block), lg:mt-0 (LoginPage.tsx:51,53,54,79,84)
Fixed sizes: min-h-[620px] on both sections, min-h-[calc(100vh-4rem)] wrapper, h-12 w-12 / h-11 w-11 brand tiles, max-w-6xl card, max-w-md form
phoneRisks: 375x667: the card is forced to min-h-[620px] inside a min-h-[calc(100vh-4rem)] wrapper, so the page is a near-full-screen card whose short form floats in vertical whitespace; with the soft keyboard open the submit button can sit below the fold (LoginPage.tsx:52,77).
No autofocus on the email field; users must tap into it (LoginPage.tsx:104-113).
Inputs are py-2.5 (~42px) and the button ~40px — acceptable but under 44px.
tabletRisks: 768–1023: single column; the max-w-6xl card spans most of the width while the form is capped at max-w-md, leaving large empty panel margins and hiding all brand copy until 1024px (LoginPage.tsx:53-54,78).
desktopNotes: Two-column card with marketing panel; the product name appears three times on one screen (h1, card, footer line) (LoginPage.tsx:61,70,73).

painPoints.issue: After sign-in every role is sent to /my-work, but maintenance-only roles have no work queue and land on an empty-state page telling them to go to Incidents; '/' already knows the right landing via HomeRedirect.

Deep link is lost on re-authentication: guards redirect to /login without carrying the original location, and expiry handlers do a full window.location reload, so after signing back in users land on /my-work instead of the record they were viewing.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:14, web/src/auth/RoleRoute.tsx:15-16 (no state/from), web/src/auth/AuthContext.tsx:59-61, web/src/api/client.ts:26-28, web/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx:42

painPoints.issue: Error and notice banners are plain divs: no role='alert'/aria-live, no aria-invalid or aria-describedby on the inputs, so screen readers get no announcement of a failed sign-in.
Disabling the inputs during submit (disabled={busy}) drops keyboard focus; only the button needs disabling.
No password visibility toggle and no self-service recovery; the only path is prose telling the user to contact an administrator.
Brand copy duplicated (product name x3, 'Caltrans · Geotechnical Services' x2, internal-use statement x2) inflates a login screen for an internal tool.
Brand mark is a text tile here but an SVG image in the app header; separator is '·' here and '|' in the header.

strengths: Session-expiry notice tells users why they were signed out, and storage access is wrapped in try/catch for hardened browsers (LoginPage.tsx:16-25).
Correct autocomplete tokens (username / current-password) and inputMode='email' help password managers and mobile keyboards (LoginPage.tsx:106-107,120).
Clear busy state on the submit button and a consistent brand focus ring on inputs (LoginPage.tsx:111,124,128-130).
Honest internal-use messaging and a defined escalation path (LoginPage.tsx:69-72,133-135).
Fully theme-aware via CSS variables so the stored theme applies before sign-in (LoginPage.tsx:51-53).

screens.name: Session validation gate (AuthGateLoading)
screens.route: Rendered in place of any ProtectedRoute/RoleRoute child while AuthContext.isInitializing is true, and on /login when a stored token exists (ProtectedRoute.tsx:13, RoleRoute.tsx:14, LoginPage.tsx:27)
screens.purpose: Block protected UI until GET /auth/me confirms the stored token and roles.
roles: Any user with a stored token (before roles are known)
primaryTasks: Wait for the session to validate

dataShown.note: Reassures the user the app is loading (AuthGateLoading.tsx:6)

dataShown.label: 'Validating ERIS session'
dataShown.note: States what is happening (AuthGateLoading.tsx:7)

dataShown.label: 'Confirming your account and access before loading operational data.'
dataShown.note: Explanatory; fine for a sub-second state (AuthGateLoading.tsx:8)

dataShown.label: Pulsing half-width bar
dataShown.note: Decorative indeterminate indicator; not a real progressbar (AuthGateLoading.tsx:9-11)

entryPoints: Automatic on app start with a stored token, for every guarded route and /login
exits: Token expired → onSessionExpired → hard redirect to /login with notice (AuthContext.tsx:77-81,49-62)
GET /auth/me fails for any other reason → token cleared silently → /login with NO notice (AuthContext.tsx:83-91)

responsive.layout: Full-viewport main with a centred max-w-lg card (AuthGateLoading.tsx:3-5).
phoneRisks: None significant; card shrinks to viewport width with px-4.

painPoints.issue: Loading state has no role='status'/aria-live or aria-busy, and the bar is a div without role='progressbar', so assistive tech receives nothing while the app blocks.
A transient network/5xx failure on /auth/me clears the token and drops the user at /login without the expired notice, so a flaky connection looks like a forced sign-out.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/auth/AuthContext.tsx:83-91 (catch clears token; no sessionStorage flag)

strengths: Prevents a flash of protected content and a redirect loop while the token is checked (ProtectedRoute.tsx:13, LoginPage.tsx:27).
Consistent brand tile and card styling with Login and Not Found screens.

painPoints.issue: RoleRoute silently redirects under-privileged users to /submissions — a page with no nav entry and not the user's home — with no 'you do not have access' feedback.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/auth/RoleRoute.tsx:19; web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:66-67 (submissions intentionally has no nav item)

painPoints.issue: Four different 'home' definitions: '/' is role-aware (/my-work or /incidents), Login always → /my-work, NotFound → /mission-center, RoleRoute fallback → /submissions.

Gating is inconsistent with the nav: /mission-center and /submissions are only ProtectedRoute although the nav hides them from maintenance roles, so Mission Center has to render an in-page refusal instead of the router handling it.
Legacy REVIEWER role is still treated as operational in the frontend while the backend marks it 'being retired'; isMaintenanceOnly is exported but never used.

strengths: Central role model mirrors backend aliases and states clearly that it is for gating only, not security (roleModel.ts:1-14).
HomeRedirect encodes the correct landing per role in one place (App.tsx:174-178).
Legacy /projects and /projects/:id URLs redirect instead of 404-ing (App.tsx:77-78,180-183).
Token expiry is proactively detected with a timer plus focus/visibilitychange re-checks (AuthContext.tsx:105-133).

screens.name: Modal dialog primitive (shared ModalDialog)
screens.route: Not routed; used by 7 dialogs: EventGroupAssociationDialog, IncidentDecisionDialogs, RoadInventoryVersionActionDialog, PasswordResetDialog, SubmissionDeleteDialog, SubmissionSectionAttachmentsDialog, WorkflowTree (grep ModalDialog)
screens.purpose: Provide one accessible overlay container (focus trap, Escape, backdrop close, scroll lock, focus restore) for every modal in ERIS.
roles: Whatever role the consuming feature exposes it to
primaryTasks: Complete or cancel a focused task without losing page context

actions.label: Explicit close button
actions.note: Each consumer must add its own; there is no standard header/close affordance (ModalDialog.tsx:112-126)

exits: onClose via Escape, backdrop, or consumer buttons; focus returns to the opener (ModalDialog.tsx:104)

responsive.layout: Default overlay: fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-center justify-center bg-black/55 p-4. Default panel: w-full max-w-xl rounded-xl p-5. Both are fully overridable strings, and 6 of 7 consumers override the panel (ModalDialog.tsx:25-26; e.g. EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:163 max-h-[92vh] max-w-6xl, WorkflowTree.tsx:127-128 items-start overflow-auto max-w-[1400px]).
breakpointsUsed: None in the primitive; consumers use max-h-[92vh] / max-h-[88vh] and max-w-* only
phoneRisks: Default panel has no max-height or overflow-y, so a tall dialog (or the on-screen keyboard) pushes buttons off-screen; only two consumers add max-h + flex-col (ModalDialog.tsx:26; EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:163; SubmissionSectionAttachmentsDialog.tsx:41).
Backdrop closes on mousedown/touchstart, so an accidental touch outside a wide panel on a small screen dismisses in-progress input (ModalDialog.tsx:108-110).
tabletRisks: Wide consumers (max-w-6xl, 1400px) fill the tablet width with p-4 margins — acceptable.
desktopNotes: Centred panel; overlay dims page. z-50 sits above the sticky header (z-20) and map stacking guards (index.css:116-124).

painPoints.issue: No default max-height/scroll on the panel; each consumer re-implements sizing, producing mixed radii (rounded-xl vs rounded-2xl) and shadows.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/ui/ModalDialog.tsx:26; RoadInventoryVersionActionDialog.tsx:34 and SubmissionDeleteDialog.tsx:32 use rounded-2xl, PasswordResetDialog.tsx:43 rounded-xl

painPoints.issue: Background content is not made inert/aria-hidden; aria-modal alone leaves the page reachable to some screen readers and to virtual-cursor navigation.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/ui/ModalDialog.tsx:112-126 (no inert, no aria-hidden on #root siblings)

painPoints.issue: No built-in title bar or close button, so every dialog invents its own header and 'Cancel' placement.

strengths: Real focus management: initial focus (with data-dialog-initial-focus override), Tab/Shift+Tab wrap, focus restored to the opener on unmount (ModalDialog.tsx:49-56,70-96,104).
Escape and backdrop dismissal are suppressed while busy, protecting in-flight saves (ModalDialog.tsx:62-68,109).
Body scroll lock with restoration and proper role='dialog' aria-modal aria-labelledby aria-describedby (ModalDialog.tsx:46-47,103,116-119).
Single reusable primitive already adopted by all seven dialogs.

crossCutting: Four competing 'home' destinations: '/' HomeRedirect is role-aware (App.tsx:177), Login always sends to /my-work (LoginPage.tsx:28,42), NotFound to /mission-center (NotFoundPage.tsx:20), RoleRoute fallback to /submissions (RoleRoute.tsx:19). All three non-root paths should navigate to '/'.

Session-expiry handling is duplicated and both copies hard-reload the SPA: web/src/api/client.ts:19-30 and web/src/auth/AuthContext.tsx:49-62 each clear the token, set sessionStorage eris_session_expired and assign window.location.href='/login', discarding router state and the deep link.

No persistent layout route: 17 pages each render <AppShell title=…> (grep '<AppShell'), so the header/sidebar remount per navigation, sidebar collapse resets (AppShell.tsx:134) and there is no place for shared shell state (toasts, unsaved-changes guard).

Dead / legacy code: web/src/pages/ProjectsPage.tsx and ProjectDetailPage.tsx are not imported by App.tsx (only they import features/projects/*, so that folder is reachable only via dead pages); roleModel.isMaintenanceOnly is never used; CSS classes .btn-brand and .surface-soft (index.css:87-104) have zero usages; --space-scale (index.css:4,79) and the data-density removal (UiSettingsContext.tsx:33) are vestiges of a removed density setting; web/public/vite.svg is unreferenced.

Vocabulary: 'Submissions' has no nav item (AppShell.tsx:66-67) yet is a redirect target and a 404 CTA; legacy 'Projects' survives in dead pages and redirects while the UI says 'Event Groups'; nav label 'Users' vs page title 'User Administration' (AdminUsersOperationsPage.tsx:173); theme names differ between header and Settings (AppShell.tsx:125-129 vs SettingsPage.tsx:4-20); 'Caltrans | Geotechnical Services' (AppShell.tsx:143) vs 'Caltrans · Geotechnical Services' (LoginPage.tsx:60,81).

Two brand marks: the header uses (AppShell.tsx:142) while Login, NotFound and AuthGateLoading use a text 'ERIS' tile in brand colour at three different sizes (LoginPage.tsx:56,80; NotFoundPage.tsx:12; AuthGateLoading.tsx:6).

Raw role codes are user-visible in the header (AppShell.tsx:157); the only humaniser is a local function in AdminUsersOperationsPage.tsx:8-10. roleModel.ts should own a roleLabel() next to assessmentStateLabel().

No shared Button component: primary buttons vary (px-4 py-2.5 font-semibold on Login/NotFound vs px-3 py-2 font-semibold on Incidents), secondary buttons vary (font-medium Sign out vs font-semibold NotFound), and the defined .btn-brand class is unused (index.css:87-95).

Alert/notice markup is copy-pasted with long color-mix class strings (LoginPage.tsx:90,96; MyWorkPage.tsx:127-128; IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:271-272) and role='alert' is applied inconsistently (present in EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:102, PasswordResetDialog.tsx:63; absent on Login, My Work, Incidents). Needs one Alert component.

Five corner radii in the shell alone: .product-card 14px (index.css:79), rounded-2xl 16px (Login/NotFound cards), rounded-xl 12px (Settings sections, dialogs), rounded-lg 8px (nav items), rounded-md 6px (buttons, inputs).

Typography: body declares 'Sora', 'Manrope' (index.css:68) but no @font-face or font link exists (index.html has none; grep found no loader), so the app renders in Segoe UI on Windows and generic sans-serif elsewhere — the intended type never ships.

Dark-theme gaps: no `color-scheme: dark` declaration (grep found none), so native <select>, checkboxes and scrollbars stay light in dark mode (e.g. the header theme select itself, AppShell.tsx:148); only ArcGIS light widget CSS is imported (main.tsx:6) so map widgets stay light; basemap follows theme only when an API key is configured (mapTheme.ts:16-19); no 'system' preference option (UiSettingsContext.tsx:26-29).

Accessibility gaps in the shell: no skip-to-content link; alsoActive nav highlight lacks aria-current (AppShell.tsx:32,40); Login and My Work errors are not announced; AuthGateLoading has no status role; nav/sign-out/theme-select targets are below 44px; focus styling mixes browser-default outlines (nav, buttons) with custom brand rings (inputs).

Mobile strategy is absent at the shell level: below lg the nav is a stacked card (AppShell.tsx:164) rather than a drawer, identity is hidden below md and theme below sm, and the lg (1024px) threshold puts portrait tablets on the phone layout.
Zero automated coverage for shell/auth/routing: package.json 'test' lists only model/unit tests and no *.test.tsx exists for AppShell, LoginPage, ProtectedRoute, RoleRoute or UiSettingsContext.

Magic layout numbers couple components: sidebar sticky top-[82px] assumes the current header height (AppShell.tsx:166); Login/auth screens hard-code min-h-[620px] and min-h-[calc(100vh-4rem)] (LoginPage.tsx:52,54,77; NotFoundPage.tsx:10; AuthGateLoading.tsx:4).
